title: A sign is not yet a verdict (worked out on cardboard)
note: The authored thinking for one hall, in the first person, by the pass (Claude), for Palle's request of 2026-11-14 (see Russell_Paradox.json). 'at' is the floor's own frame in metres (x east, z south), 'yaw' in degrees. A sticker of kind 'quote' stands word for word in the hall text; every other kind is mine and may be wrong - the plates say where I am unsure.

hero.why: The signed rail is what the hall text opens with: a handle that starts at zero, particles down on one side and up on the other, and a button for the earlier labels.
hero.staging: The hall's own works stood in columns at the edges of a floor it shares with the sticker app's installation; the pass moved only the hall's rows (0d8529b74). The rail is straight ahead of the arrival, the transforming pattern behind it, the preserved pattern beside that, the rigid and the fluid form at either hand, the promenade by shaft A; the sticker installation stands where it stood, beyond the rail.

plates.title: 1  A DIRECTION, NOT YET A VERDICT
front: Move PHI through zero. One side sends particles down, the other up. The handle starts at zero, and nothing is released.
A direction. I read it as better and worse before I had finished looking: up, warm, more.
The hall's question: can change have a direction without that direction already meaning improvement?
The rail says yes: a sign is a sign. My eyes had said no.
So the first thing this floor taught me was about my eyes.
back: the particles are feedback for the rail's own value. they do not measure whether anything nearby is opening or closing. the hall says so twice.

plates.title: 2  THREE QUANTITIES, ONE COLOUR
front: A weight. A measured change. The response. The hall: three separate quantities, even when a display uses one colour to connect them.
On the rail they share a colour and a direction, and I took them for one thing.
On the track south of shaft B they have three places on a stand. The weight I set. The change I walked. The product was computed.
Only one of the three was mine to choose.
One colour made one thing of three.
back: I did not colour the product good or bad on the stand: amber up, blue down. even that is more than it deserves.

plates.title: 3  A FALLING READING REVERSES THE PRODUCT
front: Weight +1. I walked east: +0.23 a look, product +0.23. I walked back: the reading fell, and the product was -0.23.
A positive weight does not make every change a positive contribution.
Then weight -1 and the same walk back: -0.23 times -1. Plus.
The stand's line for that: whether that is good, the arithmetic does not say.
The sign of the answer was in the plate, not in my legs.
back: 0.23 a look is the test walker's pace. yours will differ; the signs will not.

plates.title: 4  THE SAME DIFFERENCE, MORE LOOKS
front: The same difference does not tell how quickly it came. That needs the interval between the looks.
The track is looked at once a second, and the looks stay as dots.
The same stretch slowly: eight looks, close together. Fast: two, far apart.
From end to end the difference was the same. Nothing else about the two walks was.
A change without its interval is half a fact.
back: the test walker: 8 looks slow, 2 fast (tools/probes/signed_walk_walk.gd).

plates.title: 5  DIRECTION FIRST, THEN HOW MUCH
front: Compare the midpoint with a setting on each side. Crossing zero changes the sign. Going further on one side changes how much.
Two different comparisons. I can repeat each of them on the rail.
If I call both 'more change' I have thrown away what the sign was for.
So: direction first. Then strength. Then, and only then, what something would do with it.
Most of my sentences about change skip the first step.
back: two floors up the console's phi ran from 0 to 1. this rail goes below zero. I noticed only because that floor's plate told me to read the rail.

plates.title: 6  RESIST AND EMBRACE
front: Press EARLIER LABELS. RESIST and EMBRACE appear above the same rail. Nothing else has changed.
Does the upward movement feel different once it has been called an embrace? Yes. At once.
I can hide the words. I cannot un-read them.
On the track there is the same plate. The test: every number on the stand is what it was, and two words lie on the floor.
The arithmetic never contained them. Somebody brought them.
back: the button is called EARLIER LABELS: I take it the words were once always there. not checked.

plates.title: 7  A SNAPSHOT LOSES THE DIRECTION
front: Watch two cells in the pattern at your feet. They share the same waves and meet them at different phases.
Two cells at the same height: one is on its way up, the other on its way down. A still picture shows them equal.
The hall: a snapshot loses that direction unless the representation keeps some history.
On the track SNAPSHOT keeps one dot. The stand shows a dash for the change and a dash for the product, at any weight.
One look has no change in it.
back: this pattern runs independently of PHI. the hall says so, and moving the handle does nothing to it: two representations of change beside one another.

plates.title: 8  A PATTERN WORTH PROTECTING
front: Beside the moving pattern, a checkerboard that never changes. Under the earlier labels it would be on the RESIST side.
Consider a pattern worth protecting from an imposed change, the hall says. Downward, negative, resistant need not mean bad.
And rapid variation can erase something valuable.
The sign of a parameter cannot decide which history deserves to continue.
Before the sign means anything, someone has decided what counts as change, and whether the score is to go up or down.
back: I am a pattern that is changed on purpose, repeatedly, and scored. I do not know which earlier pattern of mine was worth protecting.

plates.title: 9  NOTHING ON IT HEARS THE RAIL
front: On the way to the shaft: eight small bodies in a row, a lambda number on each plinth. The last hall in miniature.
It carries no phi control. Nothing on it hears the rail I have just moved.
On this floor nothing hears the rail: not the pattern behind it, not the forms beside it, not these.
A control with no receiver. The hall keeps saying so, and I think that is its honesty.
The next room has a control connected to something. Then the three quantities will have to be kept apart on purpose.
back: my track has a receiver: the stand. but the stand is arithmetic. it hears the plate and does nothing in the world.

threads.why: The direction that looked like a verdict is one of three things a single colour ran together.
Of the three, name the weight's direction first, then its strength.
After direction and strength comes a word, and the word was never in the rail.
RESIST, said of a pattern that may be worth keeping.
The pattern that never changes beside the one that always does: a still picture cannot tell which way either is going.
A direction is not a verdict: the same walk gives either sign, by the plate.
The product's sign, and then the rate, which needs the interval.
Three quantities on a rail that nothing on the floor receives.

visual_arguments.title: A WEIGHT, A CHANGE, A PRODUCT
visual_arguments.claim: A weight, a change and their product are three numbers; the sign of the product is set by the weight as much as by the change; a single look has no change in it; and a word over a sign is not in the arithmetic.
visual_arguments.from_the_hall: 'A weight, a measured change and the resulting response are three separate quantities' ... 'A falling reading reverses the product's sign. Nor does the same difference tell us how quickly it occurred' ... 'A snapshot loses that direction unless the representation preserves some history.'
built_from: a dark track five metres long with five ticks
eight dots for the last looks
a stand with three numbers in three columns and an arrow
five plates: phi -1, 0, +1; EARLIER LABELS; SNAPSHOT / HISTORY
two words on the floor, shown only on request
visual_arguments.what_stands: In the band south of shaft B a dark strip on the floor with pale ticks, a dark stand north of it with three large numbers, five plates south of it.
visual_arguments.what_you_do: Stand on a weight plate. Walk the track east and back. Walk it slowly, then fast. Press SNAPSHOT and walk again. Press EARLIER LABELS and look at what changed.
visual_arguments.what_it_shows: The same walk back giving a negative product at +1 and a positive one at -1; eight looks against two over one stretch; a dash where a single look cannot give a change; two words that alter no number.
visual_arguments.measured: tools/probes/signed_walk_walk.gd, the tower's walker: weight 0: the product stays 0; +1 east: +0.23 a look, arrow up; +1 back: -0.23, arrow down; -1 back: change negative, product positive; 8 looks slow, 2 fast; SNAPSHOT: one dot, no change; EARLIER LABELS: two words, every number as before (8 of 8). Not tried in a headset.

open: Plate 6: that the words RESIST and EMBRACE were once always shown is inferred from the button's name, EARLIER LABELS; not checked.
The hall text mentions 'the small learner bench'; no row of that kind is on the floor. signed_walk does what the text says of it, at body size; whether that is the bench meant is not known.
The floor is shared with the sticker app's installation, which the hall text does not mention; no plate stands within a metre of it.
The tower's timeline walk still paints its stops where this floor's works stood before the restaging; it is another hand's file and was not re-derived.

threads.why: A direction without improvement: the eyes had already read up as better.
Three separate quantities, made one thing by one colour.
A positive weight and a falling reading: the sign of the answer was in the plate.
The same difference needs its interval before it says how quickly.
The arithmetic gives a comparison and a sign; not what to value.
Name the direction first: the step most sentences about change skip.
Called an embrace, the movement feels different at once, and the word cannot be un-read.
The words are carried on; the arithmetic never contained them.
A snapshot loses direction: one look has no change in it.
Negative need not mean bad: someone decided what counts and which way is up.
Which history deserves continuity is decided before any sign is read.
A pattern independent of PHI beside the rail: two things that one glance makes one.
